title: Finiteness of the reflection group of an abstract finite root datum
statement: Let $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ satisfy the finite-rank free lattice, perfect integer duality, finite root and coroot sets, root-coroot bijection and simultaneous reflection axioms in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Reducedness is not required. For $\alpha\in\Phi$ put $s_\alpha(m)=m-\langle m,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$, and let $W\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf Z}(M)$ be the subgroup generated by these involutions. Its action on the finite set $\Phi$ is faithful. In particular $W$ is finite. There is no assumption that the roots span $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$; empty roots and rank zero are allowed.

source.place: Appendix C.37--C.46, printed pp.615--619; specifically Proposition C.46, p.618, faithfulness and finiteness for the self-dual reflection axioms. The proof uses C.41--C.45 and does not assume finiteness of W.

proof.text: Use the lattice and simultaneous-reflection axioms of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], without its reducedness clause. The formula and $\langle\alpha,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2$ give $s_\alpha^2=1$. Under the perfect duality let $w^\vee$ act on $M^\vee$ by $y\mapsto y\circ w^{-1}$. For a generator this is $s_\alpha^\vee(y)=y-\langle\alpha,y\rangle\alpha^\vee$: evaluating on $m$ verifies the formula. Thus $\langle wm,w^\vee y\rangle=\langle m,y\rangle$. By the simultaneous-reflection axiom, the identity $(w\beta)^\vee=w^\vee(\beta^\vee)$ holds for a generator, and hence for every word by composition. Since the generators are involutions, every element of $W$ is such a word. In particular each $w$ permutes $\Phi$.

source.place: C.37--C.38, printed pp.615--616, and the dual action preceding C.46, p.618

proof.text: Put $Q=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Z}\Phi$, the smallest submodule containing the roots [def-weil-submodule-span]. Every $u\in W$ preserves $Q$, since it permutes its generators. Prove $w(m)-m\in Q$ by induction on a word for $w$, uniformly for $m\in M$. The empty word gives zero. For a reflection, $s_\alpha(m)-m=-\langle m,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha\in Q$. The multiplication step is $uv(m)-m=u(v(m)-m)+(u(m)-m)\in Q$. Closure under addition and integer scalars is part of the submodule definition.

source.place: C.45, printed p.618; the displacement induction is written out

proof.text: Let $w\in W$ fix every root. Step 1 and the root-coroot correspondence imply $w^\vee(\beta^\vee)=\beta^\vee$ for every $\beta\in\Phi$; its inverse fixes them too. Therefore, for every $m\in M$ and $\beta\in\Phi$, $$\langle w(m)-m,\beta^\vee\rangle=\langle m,(w^\vee)^{-1}(\beta^\vee)\rangle-\langle m,\beta^\vee\rangle=0.$$ This uses preservation of the perfect pairing, not that roots span $M$.

source.place: C.46, printed pp.618--619: the orthogonality calculation, using simultaneous correspondence to pass from roots to coroots

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-lattice-coroot-separation] with $I=\Phi$, $a_\beta=\beta$, $c_\beta=\beta^\vee$ and the prescribed simultaneous reflection permutations. Its finite-index-set, perfect integer pairing and injectivity hypotheses are precisely the datum axioms; it needs neither reducedness nor spanning. For $x=w(m)-m$, step 2 gives $x\in Q$ and step 3 gives zero evaluation on every coroot. If $x\ne0$, the cited separation statement supplies a nonzero evaluation, a contradiction. Hence $w(m)=m$ for every $m$, so $w=1$. If two elements act identically on $\Phi$, their quotient fixes every root and is the identity; the permutation action is injective. Its codomain is finite (there are at most $|\Phi|^{|\Phi|}$ self-maps when $\Phi$ is nonempty, and one when empty), so $W$ is finite. For empty roots $W=\{1\}$ directly; rank zero is included.

source.place: C.44--C.46, printed pp.618--619: nondegeneracy kills the displacement, followed by the finite permutation argument

proof_origin.place: Appendix C.37--C.46, printed pp.615--619; C.45--C.46 are the assembly, with C.44 supplied by the Mathlib leaf.
